title: Two layers
summary: A tip in front is the pour for the bucket behind it.

cards.text:
Put a second row of buckets behind the first.
The back row cannot see the original pour.

It only feels tips.
When a front bucket tips, that tip is a pour into the next layer.

cards.lead: The front bucket tips at moment 1 and moment 3.
lines: The back bucket gets a pour at moment 1.

question.why: Only spikes cross. The water level stays in its own bucket.
question.simpler: A quiet front bucket sends nothing backward.

question.prompt: If the front bucket never tips, the back bucket gets no pour from it.
question.why: No tip, no message, no pour.
question.simpler: Layers talk in tips, not in water levels.

recall.question: What is passed from one layer to the next?
recall.answer: Spikes. A tip in front pours into the next layer.

deeper.note: A feedforward spiking net is just this stack. snnTorch tutorial 3 wires two leaky layers so the first layer’s spikes are the next layer’s input.

paper.title: Training Spiking Neural Networks Using Lessons From Deep Learning

terms.definition: The only message one layer sends the next. The voltage stays local. The spike travels.
